description: The multi-hazard impact research team publishes a Python model for time-dependent physical damage to buildings and infrastructure under concurrent or consecutive hazards. Zenodo archives version 0.0.1 under MIT and links its public source repository. The README describes residual damage, recovery processes, changing exposure and state-dependent vulnerability, with examples including wind with flooding or an earthquake before recovery. The model can compare how hazard order and repair assumptions change asset condition in resilience simulations. No related catalogue record explicitly covers this implementation. Coverage is user-defined hazards, assets and fragility functions, not a ready-made loss database for a specific city. A limitation is that direct damage depends on the input vulnerability curves and recovery schedule; the tool’s mathematical structure does not itself validate those inputs. The linked article is an EGUsphere preprint, so peer-review status should not be overstated. The archive was not downloaded, and no scenario result was reproduced.
